text:
Alex W: Heads-up — canary against dedicated GPUs showing a perf regression on the MQA + paged-KV codepath for long sequences. Seen on rtx-dedicated-2. Throughput down ~28% at seqlen=1536, tail latency up 2x.

Mira P: Which variant? paged-attn or the new block-paged kernel?

Alex W: Looks like paged-attn with block_size=128 (kvpage layout = interleaved). Quick output from local microbench:
```
bench: ./bench/kvpage/blocksz_sweep.py --model=gpt2 --mqa=2
seqlen 512:  QPS 4500
seqlen 1024: QPS 2200
seqlen 1536: QPS 760  # was ~1050 before
seqlen 2048: QPS 420
```

Sam T: Interesting — that drop at 1536 smells like a kernel switch point. Paging overhead + extra page faults/TLB thrash. Did you collect nsys timeline?

Alex W: nsys shows a spike in memcpy and kernel stall (kv_prefetch) right after step where kv-blocks cross 1 page boundary.

Jordan L: Hypothesis: block_size=128 causes more fragmented entries when MQA splits heads -> causes more scatter loads. Try block_size=256 or compact layout (kvstripe) and see if selector should prefer non-paged kernel for seqlen>=1400.

Mira P: Agreed. Also think autotuner should consider effective tokens-per-request (batch*seqlen) not just seqlen. For small batches with very long seqlens paged path loses.

Alex W: Proposed selector rule (pseudo):
```
if model.mqa and seqlen >= 1400 and batch_size*seqlen > 4000:
    pick 'non_paged_attn' unless kv_layout == 'compact'
else:
    pick 'paged_attn'
```

Sam T: Minor tweak — use measured QPS delta from perf db to set threshold, not hard constant. We can add a quick autotune job that sweeps block_size and layout and writes best kernel into model_profile.json.

perf-bot: bench/job/2176543200 (kvpage-blocksz-sweep) finished: artifacts -> s3://redwood-qa/bench/2176543200. Comparison: canary vs baseline shows -27% perf at seqlen=1536 for blocksz=128.

Mira P: Next steps: (1) run blocksz sweep on A100 and V100, (2) run autotune that records tokens-per-request, (3) land selector change behind feature flag and run canary. I'll take (1) + (2).

Alex W: Thanks — I'll draft the selector PR and add fallback to prefetch-disabled paged kernel for latency-sensitive routes. :thumbsup:

Sam T: 👍 keep it small, we can iterate.
